subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Shelf Life Realities
description: A quick win: understand Shelf Life Realities.

hook.text: Roasted coffee doesn't expire like milk, but it does peak quickly and decline slowly.

buildup.text: Peak flavor hits 5–14 days after roasting. After three weeks, noticeable staling begins.

discovery.text: Green (unroasted) beans, however, can last 6–12 months if stored in cool, dry, dark conditions.

twist.text: Supermarket beans are often months old by the time you buy them. The roast date is rarely printed.

climax.text: Specialty roasters print roast dates. Buying within two weeks of roasting ensures peak quality.

punchline.text: Check the roast date. Freshness has a short, sweet window.

quiz.question: When does roasted coffee reach peak flavor?

details.summary: Most commercial coffee carries best-before dates 12 to 18 months out, but specialty coffee peaks within weeks. Whole beans hold up far better than pre-ground because less surface area is exposed to oxygen. Packaging technology like nitrogen flushing extends but cannot replace true freshness.
details.whyItMatters: Consumers often drink stale coffee without knowing it. A roast date on the bag is far more meaningful than a best-before date.
takeaways: Specialty coffee peaks 1 to 4 weeks after roasting
Best-before dates on commercial coffee are misleading

faq.question: Why do specialty roasters print roast dates?
faq.answer: Roast dates tell consumers exactly how fresh the coffee is, which directly correlates with flavor quality. A best-before date gives no information about when peak flavor occurs. Specialty customers want to brew within the optimal freshness window.

faq.question: Is expired coffee safe to drink?
faq.answer: Yes. Stale coffee is safe; it just tastes flat and dull. Coffee does not develop harmful bacteria because it has very low moisture content. The loss is entirely about flavor, not safety.
